Algebra I · Lesson 7.6

Parallel, Perpendicular, Comparing Lines

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Slope-intercept form and standard form each describe a single line. With two lines on one plane there are three further questions, whether they ever meet, whether they stay the same distance apart, and whether they cross at a right angle. All three are settled by comparing the two slopes, and the first one starts here.

Problem
The lines y=4x−1y=4x−1 and y=4x+7y=4x+7 are two different lines. A point lying on both has a single yy-coordinate, so its xx satisfies 4x−1=4x+74x−1=4x+7. Enter how many points lie on both lines.
Show a hint
  • Both lines have slope 44, so both sides of 4x−1=4x+74x−1=4x+7 contain the same 4x4x term. Subtract 4x4x from both sides and look at what remains.
  • The subtraction leaves −1=7−1=7, an equation containing no xx. Decide whether that statement is true or false, then count the shared points that follow.
Show the full solution
Subtracting 4x4x from both sides of 4x−1=4x+74x−1=4x+7 leaves −1=7−1=7, false for every xx, so no point lies on both lines and the count is 00​. The two slopes are equal, which is why the subtraction removes every xx term and leaves only the constants.
Problem
The lines y=3x−5y=3x−5 and y=−2x+15y=−2x+15 have different slopes. At a point on both, the two right sides are equal, so 3x−5=−2x+153x−5=−2x+15. Enter the yy-coordinate of the point that lies on both lines.
Show a hint
  • Solve 3x−5=−2x+153x−5=−2x+15 for xx first. The question asks for a yy-coordinate, so that value of xx is not the answer.
  • Adding 2x2x to both sides gives 5x−5=155x−5=15. Once xx is known, put it into either equation to get yy, and both equations should give the same yy.
Show the full solution
Adding 2x2x to both sides of 3x−5=−2x+153x−5=−2x+15 gives 5x−5=155x−5=15, so 5x=205x=20 and x=4x=4. Then y=3(4)−5=7y=3(4)−5=7​. Putting x=4x=4 into the other equation gives −2(4)+15=7−2(4)+15=7, the same yy. The slopes differ, so the xx terms do not cancel and one value of xx is left, with one yy to match.
Key idea
Two lines with the same slope are parallel or are the same line. A point lying on both y=mx+b1y=mx+b1​ and y=mx+b2y=mx+b2​ satisfies mx+b1=mx+b2mx+b1​=mx+b2​, and subtracting mxmx from both sides leaves b1=b2b1​=b2​, a statement with no xx in it. When b1≠b2b1​=b2​ it is false whatever xx is, so no point lies on both lines, and two distinct lines with no shared point are parallel. When b1=b2b1​=b2​ the two equations are the same equation, every point of one line is a point of the other, and there is one line rather than two.
Problem
Solving 5x−2y=85x−2y=8 for yy gives y=52x−4y=25​x−4, so those two equations describe one line and every point of that line satisfies both. Of the five points (0,−4)(0,−4), (2,1)(2,1), (4,6)(4,6), (6,11)(6,11) and (−2,−8)(−2,−8), enter how many satisfy both equations.
Show a hint
  • The two equations describe one line, so each listed point satisfies both of them or neither of them. That is one test per point, not two.
  • Put a point's xx into y=52x−4y=25​x−4 and compare the result with that point's own yy. The point counts only when the two agree.
Show the full solution
The points (0,−4)(0,−4), (2,1)(2,1), (4,6)(4,6) and (6,11)(6,11) all satisfy y=52x−4y=25​x−4, while 52(−2)−4=−925​(−2)−4=−9, not −8−8, so the count is 44​. One line written twice has infinitely many points on it, and a listed point still has to be one of them.
Problem
The line 9x+ky=409x+ky=40 is parallel to the line y=34x−2y=43​x−2. From 7.5 the first line has slope −9k−k9​. Enter kk.
Show a hint
  • Parallel lines have equal slopes, so set the slope of 9x+ky=409x+ky=40 equal to the slope of the other line and solve for kk.
  • The equation to solve is −9k=34−k9​=43​. Cross-multiply, keeping the minus sign attached to the 99, then divide both sides by 33.
Show the full solution
Parallel lines have equal slopes, so −9k=34−k9​=43​, which gives 3k=−363k=−36 and k=−12k=−12​. Then 9x−12y=409x−12y=40 reads y=34x−103y=43​x−310​, a different yy-intercept from −2−2, so the two lines are parallel rather than one line.
Key idea
Two lines with different slopes cross exactly once. A point lying on both y=m1x+b1y=m1​x+b1​ and y=m2x+b2y=m2​x+b2​ satisfies m1x+b1=m2x+b2m1​x+b1​=m2​x+b2​, and collecting the xx terms on one side gives (m1−m2)x=b2−b1(m1​−m2​)x=b2​−b1​. Since m1≠m2m1​=m2​ the coefficient of xx is not zero, and by chapter 4 an equation of that shape has exactly one solution, x=b2−b1m1−m2x=m1​−m2​b2​−b1​​. There is one yy at that xx, so the two lines share exactly one point however close their slopes are.

Chapter 5 counted the solutions of a system of two linear equations and found three answers, exactly one, none at all, and infinitely many. A solution is a pair (x,y)(x,y) that satisfies both equations, and such a pair is a point lying on both lines. The three panels above are those three counts drawn.

Problem
In the system 10x+4y=2610x+4y=26 and 15x+7y=3915x+7y=39, the xx-coefficient and the constant of the second equation are both 3223​ times those of the first. Enter the number of solutions the system has.
Show a hint
  • The xx-coefficients and the constants being in proportion is not enough on its own. Compare the two slopes instead, using −AB−BA​ on each equation.
  • The slopes are −104−410​ and −157−715​. Reduce both and compare them, rather than judging by how alike the two equations look.
Show the full solution
The slopes are −104=−52−410​=−25​ and −157−715​, which differ, so the lines cross once and the number of solutions is 11​. The 3223​ scaling of the xx-coefficients and the constants means nothing by itself, since the yy-coefficients are in the ratio 7447​, and all three ratios must match for the two equations to be the same line.
Problem
The system kx+8y=5kx+8y=5 and 10x+4y=710x+4y=7 has no solution for exactly one value of kk. Deciding it needs the slopes of both lines, which 7.5 reads off standard form. Enter kk.
Show a hint
  • No solution means the two lines are parallel, so their slopes are equal and their yy-intercepts are not.
  • Set −k8−8k​ equal to the slope of 10x+4y=710x+4y=7, then solve for kk.
Show the full solution
No solution means the lines are parallel, so the slopes match. The slope of 10x+4y=710x+4y=7 is −104=−52−410​=−25​, so −k8=−52−8k​=−25​ and k=20k=20​. Doubling 10x+4y=710x+4y=7 gives 20x+8y=1420x+8y=14, and the first equation has 55 on the right, so the lines are parallel rather than the same line.
Key idea
Each of chapter 5's three counts is one of the three pictures. Two lines with different slopes share one point, and that is a system with exactly one solution. Two lines with the same slope and different yy-intercepts share no point, the case 5.3 reached as the false statement 0=90=9. Two equations with the same slope and the same yy-intercept describe one line drawn twice, which is 5.3's 0=00=0, where every pair solving one equation solves the other. A count of solutions is a count of shared points.

Two lines that cross form four angles, and when all four are right angles the two lines are perpendicular. A quarter turn about the crossing point sends each line onto the other, so it sends a slope triangle under one line to a slope triangle under the other. That is enough to get the second slope from the first.

Problem
A segment from the origin to (5,2)(5,2) has run 55 and rise 22, so it lies along a line of slope 2552​. A quarter turn counterclockwise about the origin leaves the origin in place and sends (5,2)(5,2) to (−2,5)(−2,5), so the turned segment runs from the origin to (−2,5)(−2,5) along a line perpendicular to the first. Enter the slope of the turned line, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Slope is rise over run, and here both are measured from the origin out to the far end of the turned segment. Going out to that end means going left first, so one of the two is negative.
  • Divide the rise by the run and reduce, keeping the minus sign in front of the fraction. As a check, that slope times 2552​ has to come out to −1−1.
Show the full solution
The run is −2−2 and the rise is 55, so the slope is 5−2=−52−25​=−25​​. That is 2552​ flipped over with its sign changed, and the product 25⋅(−52)52​⋅(−25​) is −1−1, as it must be for perpendicular lines.
Fun fact
Euclid's fifth postulate is the assumption that through a point off a given line exactly one parallel can be drawn. Two thousand years of attempts to prove it from the other four ended in the 1820s, when Lobachevsky and Bolyai built geometries without it.
Problem
In the previous problem the perpendicular slope came out as the first slope flipped over with its sign changed. The lines 5x+6y=135x+6y=13 and 6x+cy=56x+cy=5 are perpendicular. Enter cc.
Show a hint
  • Read the slope of 5x+6y=135x+6y=13 off standard form, then flip it over and change its sign.
  • The perpendicular slope is 6556​, and the second line has slope −6c−c6​.
Show the full solution
The line 5x+6y=135x+6y=13 has slope −56−65​, so a line perpendicular to it has slope 6556​. The second line has slope −6c−c6​, and −6c=65−c6​=56​ gives 6c=−306c=−30, so c=−5c=−5​. Flipping without changing the sign would give c=5c=5, which makes the two lines parallel instead.
Key idea
The slopes of two perpendicular lines multiply to −1−1. Take a line of slope m=bam=ab​ and draw a slope triangle under it with run aa and rise bb. A quarter turn counterclockwise sends a run of aa and a rise of bb to a run of −b−b and a rise of aa, and the turned triangle lies under a line perpendicular to the first, so that line has slope a−b=−ab−ba​=−ba​. Their product is ba⋅(−ab)=−1ab​⋅(−ba​)=−1. One slope is therefore −1m−m1​ when the other is mm, the reciprocal with its sign changed.

Deciding how two lines sit takes two comparisons and no graph. Compute the slope of each line, whatever form it is written in. Equal slopes means parallel or the same line, and comparing yy-intercepts settles which. Different slopes means one crossing point, a right angle exactly when the two slopes multiply to −1−1.

Problem
One line is 6x+15y=206x+15y=20 and the other is y−4=52(x+3)y−4=25​(x+3). Enter one word, parallel, perpendicular, same or neither, for the relationship between the two lines.
Show a hint
  • Comparing two lines means comparing their slopes. One equation is in standard form and the other is in point-slope form, and neither has to be solved for yy first.
  • The slopes are −615−156​ and 5225​. Put the first in lowest terms, then multiply the two.
Show the full solution
The line 6x+15y=206x+15y=20 has slope −615=−25−156​=−52​, and y−4=52(x+3)y−4=25​(x+3) has slope 5225​. The slopes differ and their product is −1−1, so the lines are perpendicularperpendicular​. Reduce before comparing, since −615−156​ and −25−52​ are the same number but only the second one reads as the negative reciprocal of 5225​.
Problem
Four pairs of lines are listed. Pair 1 is y=3x−2y=3x−2 and y=−13x+5y=−31​x+5. Pair 2 is y=7y=7 and x=−4x=−4. Pair 3 is y=49xy=94​x and y=94x−1y=49​x−1. Pair 4 is y=−5x+2y=−5x+2 and y=−15xy=−51​x. Enter how many of the four pairs are perpendicular.
Show a hint
  • Three of the pairs can be settled by multiplying the two slopes. In the one that is left a line has no slope, so there is no product to take, and that pair has to be decided from the two lines themselves.
  • From 7.2 the graph of y=7y=7 is a horizontal line and the graph of x=−4x=−4 is a vertical one. Picture those two and read the angle where they cross.
Show the full solution
Pair 1 gives 3⋅(−13)=−13⋅(−31​)=−1, and pair 2 is a horizontal line crossing a vertical one, so both of those are perpendicular. Pair 3 gives 49⋅94=194​⋅49​=1 and pair 4 gives −5⋅(−15)=1−5⋅(−51​)=1, so the count is 22​. The product test needs two slopes, and pair 2 supplies only one.
Key idea
A horizontal line and a vertical line are perpendicular, and the test m1m2=−1m1​m2​=−1 does not apply to that pair. A vertical line has no slope, so there is no second number to multiply, and the test is available only when both lines have a slope. Same and parallel can be settled without slopes at all. Multiplying A1x+B1y=C1A1​x+B1​y=C1​ through by a constant scales AA, BB and CC together, so A2A1=B2B1=C2C1A1​A2​​=B1​B2​​=C1​C2​​ means one line written twice, while matching ratios in AA and BB but not in CC means parallel.

Chapter 7 began with one point on the plane and ends with two lines compared. Pinning down a single line takes a point and a slope. Comparing two lines takes their slopes, plus the yy-intercepts when those slopes are equal. The last two problems run that both ways, choosing a constant to force a relationship and then finding a crossing point.

Problem
The line kx+6y=11kx+6y=11 is parallel to y=23x+5y=32​x+5 for one value of kk, and perpendicular to it for a different value. Enter the value of kk that makes the two lines perpendicular.
Show a hint
  • The slope of kx+6y=11kx+6y=11 is −k6−6k​, and the other line has slope 2332​. Perpendicular is the case where the two slopes multiply to −1−1.
  • The first line needs slope −32−23​, so solve −k6=−32−6k​=−23​. The parallel value of kk is a different number and is not what is asked for.
Show the full solution
The line kx+6y=11kx+6y=11 has slope −k6−6k​, and perpendicular to a slope of 2332​ means a slope of −32−23​. Then −k6=−32−6k​=−23​ gives 2k=182k=18, so k=9k=9​. Parallel would need −k6=23−6k​=32​ instead, giving k=−4k=−4, so the two values have opposite signs.
Problem
Line gg passes through (6,1)(6,1) and is perpendicular to 4x+3y=184x+3y=18. Line hh passes through (−2,5)(−2,5) and is parallel to 4x+3y=184x+3y=18. Enter the xx-coordinate of the point where gg and hh cross, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Get the slope of 4x+3y=184x+3y=18 first. Line hh has that same slope and line gg has its negative reciprocal, and each line also comes with a point of its own.
  • The two equations are y=1+34(x−6)y=1+43​(x−6) and y=5−43(x+2)y=5−34​(x+2). Setting them equal and multiplying through by 1212 clears both fractions at once.
Show the full solution
The line 4x+3y=184x+3y=18 has slope −43−34​, so gg has slope 3443​ and hh has slope −43−34​. Setting 1+34(x−6)=5−43(x+2)1+43​(x−6)=5−34​(x+2) and multiplying by 1212 gives 9x−42=28−16x9x−42=28−16x, so 25x=7025x=70 and x=145x=514​​. Both lines give y=−75y=−57​ there. Since gg is perpendicular to 4x+3y=184x+3y=18 and hh is parallel to it, gg and hh are themselves perpendicular.

Every equation in this chapter has been a statement that two quantities are equal, and the graph of each one has been a line. Chapter 8 replaces that equal sign with << or >>. Lesson 8.1, The Basics of Inequality, starts with what those signs mean and what chapter 4's moves do to them.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Enter the slope of a line parallel to y=−7x+4y=−7x+4.
Show the solution
Parallel lines have equal slopes, and y=−7x+4y=−7x+4 has slope −7−7​. The 44 is the yy-intercept, not the slope, and two distinct parallel lines differ only in that constant.
Practice
A line is perpendicular to the line y=13x−8y=31​x−8. Enter the slope of the perpendicular line.
Show the solution
The given line has slope 1331​, and perpendicular slopes multiply to −1−1, so the other slope is −1÷13=−3−1÷31​=−3​. Flipping 1331​ without changing the sign gives 33, and 13⋅3=131​⋅3=1, not −1−1.
Practice
The lines y=5x−2y=5x−2 and y=5x+11y=5x+11 are parallel, perpendicular, the same line, or none of those. Enter one word, parallel, perpendicular, same or neither.
Show the solution
Both lines have slope 55, and the yy-intercepts −2−2 and 1111 are different, so the lines never meet and they are parallelparallel​. If the yy-intercepts were equal as well, the two equations would be the same line.
Practice
Enter one word, parallel, perpendicular, same or neither, for the lines y=35x−2y=53​x−2 and 3x−5y=103x−5y=10.
Show the solution
Solving 3x−5y=103x−5y=10 for yy gives −5y=−3x+10−5y=−3x+10, then y=35x−2y=53​x−2, which matches the other equation term for term, so the answer is samesame​. Same slope and same yy-intercept means one line, since every point on one is on the other.
Practice
Are the lines y=2x+6y=2x+6 and y=−2x+6y=−2x+6 parallel, perpendicular, the same line, or none of those? Enter one word, parallel, perpendicular, same or neither.
Show the solution
The slopes are 22 and −2−2. Since they are not equal, the lines are not parallel and not the same line, and 2⋅(−2)=−42⋅(−2)=−4 rather than −1−1, so they are not perpendicular and the answer is neitherneither​. Opposite signs alone do not make a right angle. Only a product of exactly −1−1 does.
Practice
A line is perpendicular to 2x+7y=152x+7y=15. Enter the slope of the perpendicular line, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
The line 2x+7y=152x+7y=15 has slope −27−72​, so the perpendicular line has slope 7227​​. The product of the two slopes is −27⋅72=−1−72​⋅27​=−1, which is the test for perpendicular lines.
Practice
The lines y=4x−9y=4x−9 and y=x+30y=x+30 cross at one point. Enter the xx-coordinate of that point, not the point itself.
Show the solution
Setting 4x−9=x+304x−9=x+30 gives 3x=393x=39, so x=13x=13​. Substituting back gives 4(13)−9=434(13)−9=43 and 13+30=4313+30=43, so the crossing point is (13,43)(13,43), and answering 4343 reports the yy-coordinate instead of the xx-coordinate.
Practice
The line y=kx+2y=kx+2 is parallel to 3x−4y=83x−4y=8. Enter kk as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Solving 3x−4y=83x−4y=8 for yy gives y=34x−2y=43​x−2, and parallel lines have equal slopes, so k=34k=43​​. Dividing −3x−3x by −4−4 makes the sign positive, so reporting −34−43​ is the common slip.
Practice
Consider the two equations 3x−y=63x−y=6 and y=3x−6y=3x−6. Of the six points (0,−6)(0,−6), (4,6)(4,6), (−1,−9)(−1,−9), (2,1)(2,1), (5,10)(5,10) and (−3,−14)(−3,−14), enter how many satisfy both equations.
Show the solution
Rearranging 3x−y=63x−y=6 gives y=3x−6y=3x−6, the second equation exactly, so the two describe one line and a point satisfies both or neither. Testing each, (0,−6)(0,−6), (4,6)(4,6) and (−1,−9)(−1,−9) fit while the other three do not, so the count is 33​. One line written twice still only contains the points that satisfy it.
Practice
The line cx+10y=7cx+10y=7 is perpendicular to y=54x−1y=45​x−1. Enter cc.
Show the solution
A line perpendicular to a line of slope 5445​ has slope −45−54​, and cx+10y=7cx+10y=7 has slope −c10−10c​, so multiplying −c10=−45−10c​=−54​ by −10−10 gives c=8c=8​. Checking, 8x+10y=78x+10y=7 gives y=−45x+710y=−54​x+107​, and 54⋅(−45)=−145​⋅(−54​)=−1.
Practice
The vertical line x=−4x=−4 and the horizontal line y=9y=9 cross at a right angle, even though the product of their slopes cannot be formed, since a vertical line has no slope. A third line is perpendicular to y=9y=9. Enter the slope of that third line, or the word undefined if it has none.
Show the solution
A line perpendicular to a horizontal line is vertical, and any two points of a vertical line have the same xx-coordinate, so the change in xx is 00 and the slope is undefinedundefined​. This is the pair the product rule cannot reach, since one of the two slopes does not exist to be multiplied.
Practice
For exactly one value of pp the system 5x−2y=95x−2y=9 and 15x+py=415x+py=4 has no solution. Enter pp.
Show the solution
No solution means parallel, so −15p=52−p15​=25​, giving 5p=−305p=−30 and p=−6p=−6​. Dividing 15x−6y=415x−6y=4 by 33 gives 5x−2y=435x−2y=34​, which differs from 99, so the lines are parallel and not the same.
Practice
Line ww is parallel to 7x+4y=97x+4y=9 and passes through (−4,5)(−4,5). Enter the yy-coordinate of the point where ww crosses the yy-axis.
Show the solution
Line ww has slope −74−47​, so going from (−4,5)(−4,5) right by 44 to x=0x=0 drops yy by 77, leaving −2−2​.
Practice
Line nn is perpendicular to y=53x+1y=35​x+1 and passes through (10,4)(10,4). Enter the yy-coordinate of the point where nn crosses the yy-axis.
Show the solution
Line nn has slope −35−53​, so y=−35x+by=−53​x+b, and putting in x=10x=10 and y=4y=4 gives 4=−6+b4=−6+b, which makes the yy-intercept 1010​. Using 5335​ instead of −35−53​ is the common slip, and the check is that perpendicular slopes multiply to −1−1.
Practice
Line aa is perpendicular to the line 3x+12y=203x+12y=20 and passes through (4,7)(4,7). Enter the yy-coordinate of the point on line aa whose xx-coordinate is 1212.
Show the solution
Solving 3x+12y=203x+12y=20 for yy gives slope −14−41​, so line aa has slope 44, since −14⋅4=−1−41​⋅4=−1. From (4,7)(4,7) a run of 88 gives y=7+4(8)=39y=7+4(8)=39​.
Practice
For exactly one value of tt the system 10x−15y=t10x−15y=t and 4x−6y=144x−6y=14 has infinitely many solutions. Enter tt.
Show the solution
Multiplying 4x−6y=144x−6y=14 by 5225​ gives 10x−15y=3510x−15y=35, so t=35t=35​. Infinitely many solutions means both equations describe the same line, which needs all three numbers proportional and not just the xx and yy coefficients. With any other tt the two lines have the same slope but different yy-intercepts, so they are parallel and there is no solution.
Practice
For each of k=−8k=−8, k=−2k=−2, k=0k=0, k=3k=3, k=8k=8 and k=12k=12, the equations kx+6y=21kx+6y=21 and 4x−3y=94x−3y=9 form a system. Enter how many of those six systems have exactly one solution.
Show the solution
Only the k=−8k=−8 system does not have exactly one solution, so the count is 55​. In slope-intercept form the slopes are −k6−6k​ and 4334​, equal only when k=−8k=−8, and different slopes mean exactly one crossing point. Scaling 4x−3y=94x−3y=9 by −2−2 gives −8x+6y=−18−8x+6y=−18, and −18≠21−18=21, so at k=−8k=−8 the two lines are parallel and that system has no solution.
